title: Al-Asma' al-Husna (The Most Beautiful Names of Allah)
summary: Allah has the Most Beautiful Names (al-Asma' al-Husna). Introduce your child to his Lord through them and endear Him to his heart. Choose names that resonate with him and link each name to its effect: "Al-Rahman (The Most Merciful), Al-Rahim (The Especially Merciful)" show mercy to us more than our mother; "Al-Razzaq (The Provider)" provides for every creature, even the ant; "Al-Sami' (The All-Hearing), Al-Basir (The All-Seeing)" hear our du'a and see everything; "Al-Ghafur (The Forgiving)" forgives when we err and repent. Teach him to call upon Allah by His Names: "Ya Rahman (O Most Merciful), have mercy on me; Ya Razzaq (O Provider), provide for me." Knowing the Names makes the child’s relationship with his Lord a living, close bond—not just a distant idea.
try_this: This week: Memorize three of Allah’s Names (Al-Rahman, Al-Razzaq, Al-Sami') with your child, and ask him to call upon Allah by each Name in a suitable situation during the day.
reflection_prompts: How can you connect one of Allah’s Names to a situation your child is experiencing so he feels its effect?
Which Name of Allah do you wish your child’s heart to become attached to first, and why?

review_defects.why: The Arabic name is 'As-Sami'' (with assimilation of the definite article before a sun letter). The transliteration 'Al-Sami'' is inaccurate and should be 'As-Sami''.
The common translation of 'Ar-Rahim' is 'The Merciful' or 'The Most Merciful'. 'The Especially Merciful' is not a standard rendering and may introduce an unintended nuance.
